open_points.subject: M03 ContractVersion / M05 Implementation deduplicated authoring action
open_points.text: State 0: "author a function contract or implementation ... the version with its identity — an existing one when the content is equal"; M03/M05 include `issued_by`/`issued_at` and `submitted_by`/`submitted_at` but do not say what happens on equal resubmission.
open_points.question: When an equal existing contract version or implementation is returned, are `issued_by`/`issued_at` (or `submitted_by`/`submitted_at`) always the first creator metadata, and is no new record written at all?
options: Return existing record unchanged with original actor/time and write nothing new
Return existing identity but also append a new submission/issue record
Update actor/time on the existing record
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing record unchanged (original actor/time), with no new record.

open_points.subject: M02 Slot current implementation fact
open_points.text: "A slot's current contract version is the one issued last; its current implementation is that version's current activation."
open_points.question: What is the slot's 'current implementation' fact when the current contract version has no activation yet (e.g., no admitted implementation)?
options: Fall back to an activation from an earlier contract version
Refuse any read that asks for current implementation until one exists

open_points.subject: Run lifecycle on owner stop actions (M19 with State 0 cancel/refuse)
open_points.text: State 0: "cancel a run ... the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent" and "a refusal ends the run `refused`"; M19 also says "While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running."
open_points.question: When cancel/refuse happens while other branches or node attempts are in progress, are those in-progress executions aborted immediately or allowed to conclude (while blocking further sends)?
options: Abort in-progress work immediately and end run at once
Let in-progress work conclude but block any new downstream/effect sends
Behavior differs by node kind (function vs operation)
open_points.default_guess: Block further sends immediately and mark run ended; allow already-running local work to wind down.

open_points.subject: M24 EffectApproval vs M25 StandingGrant authority choice
open_points.text: M26: "authority: the approval or the grant it used" and M24 only specifies the mismatch case: "... whose `request_digest` no longer matches ... sends under an active grant when one applies, otherwise requests a new approval."
open_points.question: If both a valid matching approved EffectApproval and an active StandingGrant exist for the same send, which authority must be used and recorded in EffectAttempt?
options: Deterministic precedence by rule (must be specified)
open_points.default_guess: Prefer the explicit approval if it matches; otherwise use grant.
